article.title: Why Cohort Analysis Reveals What Averages Hide
article.why: 理解 cohort analysis 如何把新舊客群拆開，避免整體平均掩蓋留存與客戶品質變化。
article.author: OpenAI learning editor

paragraphs.en:
Averages are useful because they compress many observations into one number. They are also dangerous because they can make different customer experiences look the same. A company may report that its overall retention rate is stable, while the newest customers are becoming much less loyal. Cohort analysis is one way to reveal that hidden change.

A cohort is a group of people who share a starting point or another meaningful characteristic. In product and marketing work, a common cohort is “customers who first purchased in the same month.” Instead of mixing everyone together, analysts compare how each starting group behaves after one month, two months, three months, and so on.

Imagine a subscription business with many long-time customers. Those older customers may have high retention because they already understand the product and have built habits around it. Now suppose a new acquisition campaign brings in thousands of customers who cancel quickly. The overall retention rate may fall only a little at first because the large base of older customers dominates the average. A cohort table, however, can show immediately that the January group retained 70% after three months while the April group retained only 48%.

This distinction matters because the business question changes. If every cohort is weakening at the same time, the company may have a broad product or pricing problem. If only recent cohorts are weak, the likely causes may include a new channel, a changed onboarding process, a different promotion, or lower-quality targeting. The same overall average can therefore point to very different actions.

Cohort analysis also helps when results improve. Suppose the company redesigns onboarding in June. Looking at the total customer base may not show much movement because most customers never experienced the new onboarding. Comparing June and July cohorts with earlier cohorts provides a cleaner view of whether the change is associated with better early retention.

The method still requires care. Cohorts can differ for reasons unrelated to the change being studied. Holiday customers may behave differently from customers acquired in a normal month. A large discount may attract people with lower willingness to pay later. Economic conditions can change. Cohort analysis is descriptive; it does not automatically prove causality.

Another design choice is the cohort definition itself. Acquisition month is useful for lifecycle questions, but it may be the wrong grouping for other decisions. Analysts might instead compare first product used, sales channel, region, employer size, or risk segment. The cohort should match the mechanism the team wants to understand.

Good cohort reporting also keeps the denominator visible. If a small cohort has a very high retention rate, the percentage may be unstable. Showing both the rate and the number of customers prevents a tiny group from looking more important than it is.

The practical lesson is simple: whenever an average represents people who started at different times or under different conditions, ask whether the average is mixing together different stories. A cohort view often does not replace the headline metric, but it gives the headline a structure. It tells you whether the business is changing for everyone, for new customers, or only for a particular segment.

Cohorts are especially helpful when growth is fast. A rapidly expanding customer base can make yesterday's strong customers look less representative of tomorrow's economics. Finance and growth teams can therefore use cohort revenue, repeat purchase, or contribution margin curves to estimate whether newly acquired customers are becoming more or less valuable over time.
paragraphs.zh: 平均值會把不同時間、不同來源的客戶混在一起。Cohort analysis 依共同起點或特徵分組，能更早看出新客留存、通路品質或 onboarding 是否改善。它是描述工具，不會自動證明因果；仍需注意季節、促銷與 cohort size。
paragraphs.ja: 平均値は異なる時期や条件の顧客を混ぜてしまいます。コホート分析では、獲得月など共通の起点で顧客を分け、同じ経過期間で比較します。新規顧客の質やオンボーディング改善を見つけやすくなりますが、因果関係を自動的に証明する手法ではありません。

vocabulary.usage: Compare customers in the same acquisition cohort.

phrases.example: The overall average can hide a change in new customers.
Define cohorts by a meaningful starting point.

phrases.explanation: 分組方式與想分析的機制一致

grammar.title: while + clause
grammar.body: while 可用來對比兩個同時成立但方向不同的情況，例如 overall retention is stable while new cohorts weaken。

grammar.title: may + verb
grammar.body: 用 may 表示分析上的可能性，避免把描述性結果說成確定因果。

quiz.question: How can older customers hide weak new-customer retention?
quiz.answer: A large stable base can dominate the overall average.
